title: 第11章 催命符第12章 退婚
content_zh:
天气很好。
柳氏一大早就往大相国寺而去。
深秋的日头懒洋洋地照着，将寺院的黄墙碧瓦晒出一层暖意。柳氏下了轿，整了整衣襟，让丫鬟们在山门外候着，自己跟着知客僧往后面禅院走去。
她来大相国寺不是一回两回了。这些年，每隔几个月就要来一趟，求符、上香、捐香油钱，出手向来阔绰。寺里的僧人都认得这位杜节度使的夫人，见了她便堆起笑脸，一路引到方丈的禅房前。
方丈了尘正在抄经，见柳氏进来，搁下笔，起身合十。
“杜夫人来了。”
柳氏还了礼，在蒲团上坐下。有小沙弥端了茶来，她接过去抿了一口，也不绕弯子，开门见山道：“方丈，我来续护身符。”
了尘看了她一眼，目光在她脸上停了片刻，若有所思。
“夫人，”他缓缓开口，“贫僧昨夜观法坛，发觉那道一直缠在你身上的鬼气，已经散了。”
柳氏端茶的手微微一顿。
“散了？”
“散得干干净净，一丝不剩。”了尘道，“夫人身上如今没有任何鬼气缠绕，护身符也不必再续了。”
柳氏放下茶盏，眉头微微皱起。
她当然知道那道鬼气是从哪里来的——孟氏。那个贱人死了八年，魂魄一直阴魂不散地缠着她，害她夜不能寐、心神不宁，这些年全靠了尘方丈的符法才压得住。如今方丈说鬼气散了，她本该高兴，可心里总觉得不对劲。
好端端的，怎么就散了呢？
“方丈，”柳氏试探着问，“那鬼气散了，是……被超度了，还是……”
“魂飞魄散。”了尘说这四个字的时候，眼观鼻鼻观心，脸不红心不跳，“贫僧的符法镇了她多年，怨气再重的鬼魂也撑不住这么久。她的魂魄已经耗尽了最后一点灵识，消散于天地之间了。”
柳氏怔了一瞬，然后缓缓地、长长地舒了一口气。
魂飞魄散。
这四个字像一把钥匙，把她心里那把锁了八年的铁锁打开了。孟氏那个贱人，终于彻底消失了。不是去投胎，不是去转世，而是彻彻底底地、从这世间消失——连来世都没有了。

她端起茶盏，将杯中已经凉透的茶一饮而尽，只觉得浑身通透，像是卸下了一块压了八年的石头。
“方丈辛苦了。”柳氏从袖中取出一张银票，放在桌上，推了过去，“这些年的香火钱，是妾身的一点心意。”
了尘看了一眼银票的面额，眼皮微微跳了一下，却没有推辞，合十道了声“阿弥陀佛”。
柳氏站起身来，忽然又想起一事，问道：“方丈，那鬼气既已散了，往后我是不是就不用再来了？”
了尘点了点头：“夫人往后不必再来求符了。不过——”他顿了顿，“贫僧多一句嘴，纵然鬼气已散，但若造了杀业，因果还在。若能多行善事、广积福德，对夫人自己和子孙后代都有好处。”
柳氏明白地笑笑，“方丈说的是，妾身还会一如既往供奉寺里的香火的。”
什么杀业太重，什么因果报应，不就是想跟她多要钱吗？
孟氏死了，只要杜若也死了，这杜府早晚是她和五娘的。还怕没钱，来寺院烧香吗？
只是那死了的杜七娘，偏偏又回来了。
柳氏有些心烦意乱。
了尘已经重新拿起了笔，蘸了墨，正要继续抄那卷写到一半的经文。
“方丈。”
content_en:
The weather is great.
Mrs. Liu went to Daxiangguo Temple early in the morning.
The late autumn sun shines lazily, giving the temple's yellow walls and green tiles a layer of warmth. Mrs. Liu got off the sedan chair, straightened her clothes, asked the maids to wait outside the mountain gate, and followed Zhike Monk to the Buddhist temple behind.
She came to Daxiangguo Temple not once or twice. Over the years, I have been coming every few months to ask for talismans, burn incense, and donate money for sesame oil. I have always been generous. The monks in the temple all recognized the wife of Du Jiedushi. When they saw her, they put on a smile and led her all the way to the abbot's Zen room.
Abbot Liao Chen was copying scriptures when he saw Mrs. Liu coming in. He put down his pen, stood up and folded his hands.
"Mrs. Du is here."
Mrs. Liu returned the gift and sat down on the futon. A young novice monk brought tea. She took it and took a sip. Without beating around the bush, she said straight to the point: "Abbott, I'll renew the amulet."
Liao Chen glanced at her, his eyes resting on her face for a moment, thoughtfully.
"Madam," he said slowly, "this poor monk looked at the Dharma altar last night and found that the ghostly energy that had been lingering on you has dissipated."
Liu's hand holding the tea paused slightly.
"Dispersed?"
"It was completely scattered, not a single trace was left." Liao Chen said, "There is no ghost energy lingering on Madam now, and there is no need to renew the amulet."
Mrs. Liu put down the tea cup and frowned slightly.
Of course she knew where that ghostly aura came from - Meng's family. That bitch has been dead for eight years, and her ghost has been haunting her, making her sleepless at night and restless. All these years, she relied on Abbot Chen's talismans to suppress her. Now that the abbot said the ghost spirit was gone, she should have been happy, but she still felt something was wrong.
Everything was fine, why did it fall apart?
"Abbott," Ms. Liu asked tentatively, "The ghost energy has dissipated. Is it... that he has been saved, or..."
"The spirit is gone." When Liao Chen said these four words, he looked at his nose and heart, his face not red, his heart not beating. "The poor monk's spell has suppressed her for many years, and no ghost with more resentment can hold on for so long. Her soul has exhausted the last bit of spiritual consciousness and dissipated between heaven and earth."
Ms. Liu was stunned for a moment, and then slowly and deeply breathed a sigh of relief.
The soul is gone.
These four words were like a key, opening the iron lock in her heart that had been locked for eight years. That bitch Meng finally disappeared completely. Not to reincarnate, not to reincarnate, but to completely disappear from this world - not even the next life.
She picked up the tea cup and drank the already cold tea in the cup. She felt that her whole body was refreshed, as if a stone that had been weighed down for eight years had been lifted off.
"Thank you, Abbot, for your hard work." Mrs. Liu took out a banknote from her sleeve, put it on the table, and pushed it over. "The incense money earned over the years is a little bit of my heart."
Liao Chen glanced at the denomination of the bank note and his eyelids twitched slightly, but he did not refuse and said "Amitabha" with his palms together.
Mrs. Liu stood up and suddenly thought of something again and asked, "Abbott, now that the ghost spirit has dissipated, do I not have to come again in the future?"
Liao Chen nodded: "Madam, you don't have to come to ask for talismans in the future. But -" he paused, "the poor monk said one more word. Even if the ghost spirit has dissipated, if he has created murderous karma, the cause and effect will still be there. If you can do more good deeds and accumulate merit, it will be good for you and your descendants."
Mrs. Liu smiled understandingly, "What the abbot said is that I will continue to offer incense in the temple as always."
What kind of killing karma is too heavy, what kind of karmic retribution, aren't you just trying to get more money from her?
If Meng is dead, as long as Du Ruo dies too, sooner or later the Du Mansion will belong to her and Wuniang. Are you still worried about not having enough money to come to the temple to burn incense?
But the dead Du Qiniang happened to be back again.
Mrs. Liu was a little upset.
Liao Chen had already picked up the pen again, dipped it in ink, and was about to continue copying the half-written scripture.
"Abbott."
